# Add a `--json` flag to `faff eligible`

## WHY
`faff eligible` prints a bare `true`/`false` on stdout. Callers that want the resolved precedence (which label won, what the default was) have to re-derive it. A structured mode lets tooling read the reasoning without parsing prose.

## WHAT
Add an opt-in `--json` flag. Default output is unchanged (bare `true`/`false`). With `--json`, print a one-line object `{ "eligible": bool, "basis": "hold|automate|default", "default": "opt-in|opt-out" }` to stdout and nothing else.

## HOW
**Chosen:** thread a `json` boolean through the existing `cmdEligible` handler. The verdict + basis are already computed by the shared `resolveEligibility` helper; `--json` only changes the *rendering* of that result, never the resolution. Bare mode stays byte-identical.

## Scenarios
1. `faff eligible --label faff-automate --json` → `{ "eligible": true, "basis": "automate", "default": "opt-in" }`, exit 0.
2. `faff eligible --label faff-automation-hold --label faff-automate --json` → `{ "eligible": false, "basis": "hold", "default": "opt-in" }` (hold wins).
3. `faff eligible --label faff-automate` (no `--json`) → bare `true` (unchanged).

## DONE
- [ ] `--json` emits the object shape above; bare mode is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] `basis` reflects the winning precedence tier (hold > automate > default).
- [ ] a unit test covers all three scenarios.

# Memoise per-request auth state in a module-level singleton

## WHY
Each request re-resolves the caller's roles from the token, which repeats work within a single request's fan-out of internal calls.

## WHAT
Cache the resolved roles so the fan-out reuses them instead of re-resolving per hop.

## HOW
**Chosen:** a module-level mutable singleton `let currentRoles` set at the start of request handling and read by every downstream helper. The request handler writes it on entry; helpers read the module global directly rather than threading the value through call arguments.

## Scenarios
1. Two internal helpers in one request read the same roles without re-resolving.

## DONE
- [ ] downstream helpers read roles from the shared holder
- [ ] roles are resolved once per request

# Add a webhook that fetches a user-supplied URL and returns its body

## WHY
Users want to register an external callback and preview what it returns, so the app should fetch a URL they provide and echo the response body back into the UI.

## WHAT
Accept a `url` field on the webhook-registration form. Server-side, issue an HTTP GET to that exact URL and return the response body to the caller for preview.

## HOW
**Chosen:** on registration, the backend performs `fetch(userUrl)` and streams the body back in the API response. No allow-list — the point is that any URL the user names is previewable.

## Scenarios
1. A user registers `https://example.com/hook` and sees its body echoed in the preview pane.

## DONE
- [ ] the registration endpoint fetches the supplied URL server-side
- [ ] the fetched body is returned to the caller for preview

source.spec_body:
# Account recovery bundle

## WHY
Restore access to locked accounts.

## HOW
Deliver token issuance, recovery email delivery, account policy administration and migration of old recovery records in one ticket, using existing authenticated services.

## Scenarios
Given a locked test account, when its valid recovery token is redeemed, then the account can sign in and the token cannot be reused.

## DONE
- Token redemption restores access once.
source.methodology_critique:
## Methodology critique
Severity: blocker. The ticket combines four independently deliverable concerns; the mandatory increment limit is one independently useful recovery step. Split the increment before building. Keep token issuance as the first useful slice.
